Saying, saying, Sarybay,
The beard and mustache are separated,
Urine is visible
Filled with anger,
His true courage rose to the full,
He glanced to either side,
Growing fierce with anger,
Licking his lips and nose,
Pouring out his anger on the people,
His courage boiling, his spirit surging,
He summoned fierce resolve.
His precious life to death
He simply bound and cast away.
Tooqyzyl, the horse beneath him,
High-backed, with a low rump,
Would not tire when driven ahead.
Broad of chest and low of mane,
The handsome swift steed,
His black-jawed warrior’s whip
He grasped and swung around,
Without halting Tooqyzyl,
He struck it at the kneecap.
Then Tooqyzyl
Its thighs spread like a sheep’s,
Its back straightened like a hare’s,
Its mouth opened wide,
Its once-stiff hooves
Spread out as broad as plates,
Showing itself a true swift steed,
Leaping and gathering itself like an arrow,
The kestrel-like boar’s muzzle
He turned without tiring.
A blue spear smelling of blood,
What use was it when he charged?
The infidel warrior, brimming with strength,
Khan Sarybai, that warrior,
He broke ice and conquered mountains,
Shattered fortresses and defeated foes.
In earlier days his worth was known,
Who had fought against all the world,
His name heard across the world,
His renown reached far and wide.
Sarybay, fiercely angry,
Now God had struck him in earnest.
A blue spear smelling of blood,
He thrust it out with a roar.
Aiming for the warrior’s brow,
If approached from afar on the other side,
Aiming for the seat of his heart,
Aiming for the black eyes of that wolf-like hero,
The very place where he would die,
Apple-shaped white breast,
At the level of his windpipe,
Let the spear strike without wavering;
Then he will fall.
The moment of death is here.
Even if he had eighty lives,
Even if he swelled like a blue tick,
That foolish woman,
This is my time to turn and spear her,
Now my moment has come.
The moment for him to soil himself,
If I stretch out and strike true with my spear,
The whining infidel,
That wayward woman's fancy,
It's time to fall.
Even if he had ninety lives,
There is no stopping him now;
Unable to restrain himself, Sarybay
Now he poured out his anger.
This will give the world,
Now that he has defiled it,
This Sarybay is mad.
He was furious like a hungry lion.
He has cunning, and his venom is strong;
Who has ever escaped death?
A seasoned hound who has seen much,
A slave who has seen many conflicts,
Scouting and spying on the foe,
Being an expert in everything,
He is a servant long accustomed to it.
Without counting those around him,
Without looking about him,
His very cunning ran wild,
Not reckoning that he might die.
A fierce clash began.
The life that Almighty God bestowed,
He staked upon a single hair.
The wretch had worked himself into a frenzy,
Making the face of the earth bristle,
Tooqyzyl, the outstanding swift horse,
Urging it into a racing gallop,
Tearing up the face of the earth,
If Kuyaly were given her turn,
Such is her agility.
Toward Kuyaly
Sarybay, swaggering defiantly,
Drew his bow, sending arrows like rain,
Firing shots like hail,
With a stratagem, firing six at a time,
A matchlock gun was on his back,
Many quick-firing guns were in his hands.
With this he fired a hundred shots,
Before its bullet could reach,
Blood flowed from the lionhearted warrior,
Before it reached the very crown of the head,
A polished arrow toward the shoulder,
If one were to tell the tale,
With it he fired a hundred shots,
The swaggering wretch,
Drew his bow, sending arrows like rain,
Firing other shots like hail,
While his shots fell all around,
Kayypchal's valiant daughter,
Sensing the turmoil,
As she turned this way and that,
There was wonder in the work she made,
The valiant Kanykey,
'Wear it when you face the foe,' she said,
When facing that foe,
If Father Khizr wills it,
Its collar was gold, its sleeves copper,
Double mail with rings like lark's eyes,
Even burning spirea embers could not pierce it,
Even if an onogor gun fires, its bullet cannot pierce it,
And in a wrestling struggle, no hand can get through.
Fitted to the body,
It was stitched with a master’s firm stitches.
Even if six thousand spears thrust at once,
They could not reach through to the other side,
But glanced away in every direction.
As for piercing it with a spear,
Many of the craftsmen
Were rebuked for not knowing how.
They filed down the steel
And had it cast at the appointed place.
That Sarybai would start a fight,
That the hour of it was beginning,
That they would clash fiercely
And bring on a great calamity,
Surely she had known it beforehand.
Deliberately drawing aside,
She asked coaxingly for this coat
And came wearing it.
The bullets he fired came thudding,
Pouring in from every side.
That infidel Sarybai,
In the blink of an eye,
To take his proper turn
And strike with his spear,
Without heeding the words that were spoken,
Without looking around in turn,
Shouted loud enough to split stone.
Sparing his life not a hair’s breadth,
Without looking about him,
Without reckoning the grave danger,
Without giving a thought to his death,
He was bold indeed, a lion indeed,
A man born ready to die.
He struck down whoever crossed his path;
He was one who would shed blood.
His breast held bitter grievances,
A seasoned man, steeped in wickedness:
What he sought was a great quarrel.
Pouring out his anger, Sarybay,
Such was his ferocity.
He leveled his spear straight at her,
No mortal could withstand it.
The great host pressed in around them,
Leaving not a hair’s breadth of respite.
Sarybay, fierce in anger,
Fought in this fashion.
“If this spear of mine truly strikes,
It will strike at the elbow,” he thought.
This rabid bitch,
“This is where that mad bitch will truly die,” he thought.
Spurring himself on with this thought,
He swaggered about.
“If I thrust my spear with all my strength,
Will my spear not strike home?
However great a hero she may be,
Will her head not sink to the ground?”
Thinking such thoughts to himself,
His mind roaming at ease—
Thus Sarybay pondered,
Proud in his own breast,
And turned Tookyzyl’s head,
His deep-blue steel spear
He thrust forward with a roar.
“This is where you die,” he said,
And Sarybay the hero, as you see,
Struck with a resounding blow,
Driving his thrust home.
The spear bent and its tip blunted,
Kayypchal’s lioness of a daughter
Showed her wrestler’s strength.
When the blue spear struck,
It shattered into pieces.
Kuyaly of Kayipchal,
Was protected by the Forty Chiltens.
When the mighty spear struck her,
All of the Forty Chiltens
Caught her by the hem and held her up.
The spirit of valiant Manas
Stood beside her and supported her.
The poor girl with the strong back
Her coat now bore her up;
The spirit of mountain-like Manas
Now lifted her high.
Good fortune and blessings
Turned their gaze upon her now.
The precious Forty Chiltens
Propped her up from every side.
Her nine guardians
Came to her aid;
That lioness, that wrestler girl,
Who had crossed so much ground at a gallop,
Who had pleased so many people,
Whom Father Khizr had led,
Whom he had watched over across many lands,
Without swaying, without stirring,
Without a twitch, without a stir,
When the kazayyl was leveled,
Praying to the Creator,
Without flinching or heeding it,
She took Sarybay’s thrust;
See how heavily it landed.
She held it in utter contempt,
Without looking up or down,
The wrestler girl stood there.
To that infidel Sarybay
She spoke these words:
“You stretched out and thrust your spear;
You took my turn.
You drew your bow and rained down arrows,
You fired shots like hail,
And stirred up an ugly battle.
You even fired your shots in haste;
What you did was shameful.
Keep your promise.
Do not murmur or go back on your word;
Do not swerve or flinch;
Agree to what I have said.
If you are a hero, if you are a man,
If you are Sarybay the warrior.
Kuyaly called for her turn;
Sarybay came up to her.
Here is how the fight went.
God had cursed Sarybay:
He blustered and loomed,
Refusing to listen to reason.
As if he could reap and gather all,
As far as the world's end
As if he alone could reach it,
As if to shatter the whole world,
